extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature (scientists, geologists, geographers, university administrators, and instrument purchasers)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and expectations for scientific exploration/geological reports and related geography books, and standards for instruments and laboratory training as discussed in reviews, notices, and adverts. Focuses on adequacy of observations, use of sources, accuracy of data, and appropriate presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of observational basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Were the few months of rapid and necessarily imperfect and incomplete observation sufficient to justify the addition of all these volumes to the ever-growing mass of geological literature?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should ensure the temporal and spatial extent of their observations justifies extensive publication; limited, rapid reconnaissance should not be used as the basis for large multi-volume conclusions. If observations are scanty, limit scope or flag as preliminary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of unwarranted theoretical disquisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: American geological explorers often 'cannot simply describe what they have seen, but must launch out into theoretical disquisitions and systematical discussions, for which there has often been but slender basis in their own work.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve broad theoretical/systematic interpretation until supported by adequate data; do not extend discussion beyond what the observations can reliably sustain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness and prioritizing original observations
rubrics_metrics.description: The really valuable original observations are often practically buried out of sight in huge quartos; the books are heavy alike for the hand and the head and take up a large amount of space on library shelves where they are comparatively seldom consulted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present the most important original results clearly and accessibly; avoid excessive amplification or publication formats that obscure core findings. Prefer concise presentation that highlights new, significant observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigour in physiographical discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: When one reflects how difficult are the problems of physiographical development... one is amazed at the confidence with which the physiography of vast territories is here disposed of.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physiographical conclusions require patient, detailed local topographical knowledge and careful research; avoid dogmatic, sweeping statements based on rapid or limited surveys ('not by surveys of fifty square miles a day').

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of trustworthy and up-to-date sources; author familiarity
rubrics_metrics.description: The information is neither very trustworthy nor up-to-date. The author does not appear to have any personal knowledge of the country, nor has he made himself sufficiently acquainted with what has been written on the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should be personally knowledgeable or thoroughly review and incorporate the current literature; check older sources against more precise modern surveys and correct earlier errors rather than repeating them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain geographic focus and avoid irrelevant material
rubrics_metrics.description: The geographical theme is frequently lost sight of altogether under the heaps of irrelevant topics that are dragged in; fully one-fifth of the whole book is made up of generous extracts from irrelevant sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the narrative and discussion focused on the geographic/scientific subject; avoid large blocks of irrelevant quotation or digressions that dilute the primary contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of factual details (elevations, place names, maps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of incorrect factual details: elevations (Yamdok Lake given as 13,900 ft or 13,800 ft instead of 14,350 ft), Lhasa elevation mis-stated, and map claims such as treating an old sketch-map as 'the best we possess.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify numerical data (elevations, coordinates), place names, spellings and mapping claims against the most reliable surveys and primary sources (e.g., recent survey work), and correct earlier inaccuracies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful attribution and checking of historical claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The author goes beyond his authority when he credits Sir Clements Markham with a statement he did not make (e.g., that the Chinese general sacked Kathmandu).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm historical assertions and attribute statements accurately. Do not over-attribute or misrepresent the claims of other scholars; check primary sources where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of observation and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism that observers amplified notes with physiographical discussions for which there was often but slender basis; 'It is not by surveys of fifty square miles a day that these problems are to be solved.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly distinguish reported observations (data) from broader interpretative or theoretical claims, and label speculative parts as such. Ensure interpretations are proportional to the quality and quantity of observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument quality and certification (Kew Observatory test)
rubrics_metrics.description: All the above instruments will pass the Kew Observatory test. Kew Certificates, if desired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruments intended for observational work (meteorology, astronomy, etc.) should meet recognized institutional standards and obtain certification (e.g., Kew Observatory) to ensure reliability and comparability of measurements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardization and artificial aging of measurement standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Both bars and tapes standardized and artificially aged at the National Physical Laboratory; as used by the Ordnance Survey and Coast and Geodetic Survey, U.S.A., etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use measurement standards that have been standardized and artificially aged by national laboratories (e.g., NPL) for high-precision surveying and metrology to ensure consistency and long-term stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical training should combine theory and practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Statistical and Biometrical Laboratory 'provides a complete course of training, not only in the theory, but practical of Statistics. Instruction is given in the exhibition, calculation (medianical and arithmotical), and use of statistical quantities.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statistical education/programs should include both theoretical lectures and practical exercises (calculation of central tendencies, use of statistical quantities), hands-on use of mechanical integrators/calculators, and support for advanced students' research.
